dedupe_keys.name: italian municipal solid waste cost and collection panel by municipality 2016 2022

description: This table gives the cost of collecting and treating household waste in several thousand Italian municipalities, year by year, alongside how much of each waste fraction they collected. The producer is Giacomo Di Foggia, who deposited the file on Zenodo without a written description; its contents were read directly for this entry. Coverage is 31,294 municipality-years for 5,512 municipalities in all 20 regions from 2016 to 2022. Columns give total, collection, sorting, disposal, treatment, street sweeping and general costs per inhabitant and per kilogram; tonnes of organic, green, paper, glass, wood, metal, plastic, electronic, textile and unsorted waste; the separate collection rate; whether a pay-as-you-throw tariff applied; and context such as population, density, altitude, coastal or island location, tourism intensity, income and the regional shares of landfill and incineration. The file is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the record gives no source statement or data dictionary, so units must be read from column names, and not every municipality appears in every year. Simulation uses: estimating cost functions for waste collection, testing tariff and separate collection policies, and planning service capacity across municipalities. Related records: the Eurostat municipal waste statistics (data-eurostat-env-wasmun) give national totals.
name: Italian municipal solid waste cost and collection panel by municipality (2016-2022)
schema_summary: One row per municipality-year: total, collection, sorted, disposal, treatment, sweeping and general costs in euro per inhabitant and euro cents per kg; tonnes by fraction (wet, green, paper, glass, wood, metal, plastic, WEEE, textile, other sorted, unsorted, total); sorted share; PAYT tariff flag; GDP per capita; population, area, density, altitude, coastal, island, urbanisation and tourism intensity; regional landfill, incineration and sorting shares; HICP
